messages:
Marta: Quick syncwe need to finalize the layer-profiling plan before we ship mixed FP8/INT8+4bit lanes. Main goal: detect per-layer quality cliff and provide fast rollback.

Jia: I ran the microbench yesterday. FP8 kernels are ~1.9x faster on A100 for dense attention but 4bit has weird headwise variance on some lm-heads.

Owen: Can we make the runtime prefer per-layer INT8 for problematic layers and FP8 elsewhere? That would be a hybrid schedule driven by per-model profile.

Samir: That's the plan, but we need a compact profile format and a safe semantics for runtime fallback. If a layer isn't in the profile, default to conservative INT8.

Ravi: Profile format sketch: list of layer entries: layer_id, preferred_precision, qual_delta_estimate, perf_gain_estimate, confidence. Keep max 256 entries to limit size.

Jia: Also include calibration metadata (zero-point offsets, scale version) and a seed for quant noise so evals are reproducible.

Marta: Good. Ops question: how do we deploy updated profiles? Atomic update via model-versioned artifact and an activation window? Avoid mid-flight inconsistency.

Owen: We can stage profile as model artifact v1->v2 with activation timestamp. Runtime checks model_version + profile_version before executing. If mismatch, treat as no-profile (INT8).

Samir: Telemetry needs to tie divergence back to layer-level decisions. We should record per-request: applied_profile_hash, layer_precision_map, token_divergence_vector, and golden-suite-label if sampled.

Jia: Token divergence vector could be large. Summarize to histogram buckets (0, 1e-6..1e-3, 1e-3..1e-2, >1e-2) plus 90/95/99 percentiles.

Ravi: For canarying: proposed multi-stage rollout: 1) offline sims & shadow on small sample, 2) shadow ~2% global + 20% on selected customers, 3) split traffic 50/50 for low-risk endpoints, 4) full route. Each stage requires golden-suite pass and divergence tails below threshold.

Marta: Define concrete thresholds. Suggest median divergence < 1e-4, 99p < 5e-3, golden-suite pass >= 98%. Also limit hallucination regressions to <0.5% absolute.

Owen: Those numbers look tight but reasonable. We'll need A/B tests with temperature sweeping since sampling noise increases at higher temps.

Jia: Implementation detail: sampling seeds. When comparing samples between precisions, we should use the same RNG sequence where possible to reduce variance from sampling. Use seeded top-k sampling deterministically for evals.

Samir: For production compare we cannot seed real user traffic. So rely on deterministic metrics (n-gram overlap, semantic similarity embedding distance) plus golden prompts.

Marta: Ops rollback knobs: 1) region-level killswitch (force INT8 routing), 2) model-version freeze (reject profile activations), 3) per-customer opt-out header. SRE must be able to flip within 30s.

Ravi: Runtime cost concern: per-request precision checks add CPU work. We should cache decision per-endpoint+model+prefix-hash for short TTL (5m). Also memoize layer-precision maps.

Jia: Cache keys must include precision tag and profile hash to avoid KV prefix reuse across precisions. Otherwise we risk using FP8 KV with INT8 execution.

Owen: Agree. We'll add a precision_tag to KV metadata and bump serialization version. Migration: when profile activates, invalidate cache for cohorts under canary. Rewarm job will run warmup queries.

Samir: Security/compliance: for private deployments, customers may require that profiles are signed. Add signature field and verify against customer public key during activation.

Marta: Nice. Also add tamper-evidence in profile artifact (hash in model manifest).

Jia: Testing matrix: evals per (precision combo x prompt length x temperature x domain). That's large. We'll sample smartly: more coverage for long-context and multi-turn dialogs.

Ravi: We should track regressions by signal type: lexical (BLEU/ngram), semantic (embedding cosine), and safety (hallucination/safety-detector). Weight them in a composite score for gating.

Samir: Composite score proposal: 50% semantic, 30% lexical, 20% safety. Set canary pass if composite delta < 0.015 and safety regression < 0.005.

Marta: Put all that in the canary config template. Owen, can you produce a PR for the rollout infra to accept quality hooks and composite scoring?

Owen: On it. I'll include a shim for offline sim runner to compute composite score.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: canary-quality-hook v2.0 -> staging.

Jia: One more operational note: profiling jobs should run on a dedicated perf infra to avoid noisy neighbors, use same GPU microcode and driver versions as prod.

Ravi: And track hardware-specific deltas; some kernels behave differently on older driver stacks. Store per-hardware-profile in the profile artifact.

Samir: I'll start drafting the runbook with explicit rollback steps and dashboard links (token-divergence heatmap, profile-activation log, golden-suite trend).

Marta: Great. Next steps: Owen -> PR for quality hook + shim, Jia -> sampling matrix and deterministic-eval harness, Ravi -> profile schema + signing, Samir -> runbook + dashboards. Sync EOD tomorrow.

Jia: Acknowledged.

Owen: ETA EOD.

Ravi: Will upload schema spec by EOD.

Samir: Runbook draft EOD.

Marta: Thanks team, talk tomorrow.
